summary.short: H.B. 418 (Utah Digital Choice Act, new ch. 75) covers social media services, meaning public sites or apps with account-holder content, for users located in Utah. On request, a service must provide a consumer's personal data, including the social graph, in portable, usable form. Social media companies must offer a transparent, third-party-accessible interoperability interface that lets users share personal data across designated services. Most provisions take effect 1 July 2026.
summary.long: H.B. 418 (Utah Digital Choice Act, new ch. 75) covers social media services, meaning public sites or apps with account-holder content, for users located in Utah. On request, a service must provide a consumer's personal data, including the social graph, in portable, usable form. Social media companies must offer a transparent, third-party-accessible interoperability interface that lets users share personal data across designated services. The interface must use an open protocol, be offered on non-discriminatory terms, be documented, and may carry a reasonable fee for requests above company-set thresholds. Shared data requires user consent and reasonable security. Inferences, proprietary algorithms and certain proprietary-format data need not be provided. The Division of Consumer Protection enforces the chapter, may impose administrative fines and seek civil penalties of up to $2,500 per violation, and may identify open protocols that give companies a rebuttable presumption of non-discriminatory access. Violating an order carries a civil penalty of up to $5,000 per violation. Most provisions take effect 1 July 2026; section 13-75-301 takes effect 7 May 2025.

notes: Sections 1 and 2 restate amended sections in full; brackets mark deletions and renumbering, so unmarked restated text is not annotated as new. Section 10(2) gives 13-75-301 an effective date of May 7, 2025, while the rest of the bill takes effect July 1, 2026 (Section 10(1)); this is stated expressly, not an inconsistency. Obligations under Part 2 address social media companies and social media services as classes, without named firms, so no entity rows are given for them. Section 13-75-302(1) limits enforcement to existing budget allocations.
